clue.text: It's when one gets cross that counts

definitions.text: It's when one gets cross that counts

parts.words: It's when one gets cross that counts
parts.note: the cross is not anger but the X a voter marks on a ballot paper, and the counting is of those votes nationwide

explanation.surface: A grumpy remark that the only time anyone pays attention is when you lose your temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' tempts as anger; it is the mark on a ballot, and 'counts' is the tally of votes after polling day.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationwide vote to choose a parliament is the occasion when ballot marks are made and tallied.

clue.text: Movie to turn novel's sex appeal back to include muscle

parts.note: a go is one's turn in a game
novel means new
IT is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: the word for back takes the word for muscle inside it

parts.note: hind means back, as in hind legs
thew is an old word for muscle or sinew

explanation.surface: Someone decides to adapt a book's sensuality for the screen by adding some muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is a noun here, one's go in a game, and IT is old slang for sex appeal; 'to include' signals the container at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1939 Civil War epic starring Vivien Leigh is a famous film.

clue.text: One that's cracked shell?

definitions.meaning: a person who is cracked is mad, slang for a crazy person
the casing around a nut kernel, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: A crazy person is called cracked, and the hard outer covering of a walnut is a shell.

clue.text: Elevate underworld to cause a lot of trouble

definitions.text: to cause a lot of trouble

parts.note: to elevate is to raise
hell is the underworld of the damned

explanation.surface: Lifting up the realm of the dead would certainly create havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for making a great commotion or causing an uproar.

clue.text: Soldier that's enlisted to pass up straight thinking

indicators.note: the soldier is enlisted, taken into the ranks of the other word
in a down clue, up means the word for pass is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A recruit signs up rather than miss the chance to think clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like a verb; it is a mountain col, and 'up' reverses it because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning that proceeds soundly step by step is clear, rational thought.

clue.text: Involved man in clue for "brightness"

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter explains that a man is involved in the clue for a word meaning brightness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' scrambles MAN, IN and CLUE into the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, the intensity of light emitted from a surface is its measurable brightness.

clue.text: Emblematic one in group with branches in the Lebanon

definitions.text: Emblematic one in group with branches in the Lebanon

parts.words: Emblematic one in group with branches in the Lebanon
parts.note: group with branches sounds like a company with offices but means trees; one tree is the national emblem on the Lebanese flag

explanation.surface: A flagship firm among companies with branch offices in Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' suggests a bank or a chain of shops; it means boughs, and the emblem is the green tree in the middle of Lebanon's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree on the Lebanese flag is the national symbol, a conifer of the mountains there.

clue.text: I hang about to take drug in a perfect world

indicators.note: the word for hang about takes the drug inside it

parts.note: to dally is to linger or hang about
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone loiters to take drugs, imagining a perfect world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' puts E inside DALLY, after the plain I.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning under the best possible circumstances, if things were as one wished.

clue.text: Poisonous gas used briefly in knotwork?

definitions.text: Poisonous gas used briefly in knotwork?

parts.words: Poisonous gas used briefly in knotwork?
parts.note: the gas is written briefly by its chemical formula, and those characters, read as letters, sit in the middle of the word knotwork

explanation.surface: A toxic fume momentarily employed by someone tying knots.
explanation.walkthrough: The gas's formula is NO2; spell it NO TWO and it sits inside kNOTWOrk.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown toxic compound of one nitrogen atom and two oxygen atoms, a common pollutant.

clue.text: Naught comes from drink that's inherently watery

indicators.note: inherently means in its very core, so the watery word goes inside the drink

parts.note: nog is an eggy or strong drink
watery means thin, of soup or beer

explanation.surface: Nothing good comes from a weak drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naught' is zero, not wickedness; the drink nog is eggnog or a strong ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Naught means zero, not a single thing.

clue.text: Dew and mist are confused in US heartland

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so the letters of both words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters mix up dew and mist across the American interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are confused' rearranges DEW and MIST together.
explanation.definitionFit: The central northern states of America, such as Iowa and Ohio, are its agricultural heartland.

clue.text: Energy input required to make roller move back and forth

indicators.note: input means put in, so the energy symbol is placed inside the roller

parts.note: a roller is a long rolling wave at sea
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A machine needs an energy supply to make its roller oscillate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roller' looks mechanical; it is a breaker at sea. 'input' puts E inside WAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To weave is to sway or zigzag, as a boxer or a car in traffic does.

clue.text: Most important love for English to voice

indicators.note: love for English means the zero letter takes the place of the E

parts.note: central means principal or most important
love is zero in tennis, hence O

explanation.surface: A primary affection felt for England, given expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the E of CENTRAL for O, giving CONTRAL, then TO is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest female singing voice, a part in choral music.

clue.text: Ram receiving present gets on immediately

indicators.note: the ram word receives the present word inside it

parts.note: a tup is a ram
present means here
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ram given a gift promptly climbs aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A tup is a dialect word for a ram, mainly British farming usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adverb meaning straight after that, at once.

clue.text: Bounded over steps to be very vexatious

indicators.note: over means covering, so the bounded word goes over and around the steps word

parts.note: pent means shut in or bounded
a stile is a set of steps over a fence

explanation.surface: Someone leapt across the steps and became extremely irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounded' looks like leapt; it means confined. A stile is a set of steps over a fence or wall, common on British footpaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent can mean annoying or troublesome, like a pest.

clue.text: Glaswegian runner's part in muscly deeds

indicators.note: part in says a portion of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A Scottish athlete's share in feats of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it is the river that runs through Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through Glasgow; rivers run in crossword language.

clue.text: Member of fourth estate or fifth?

definitions.meaning: the fourth estate is the press, so one of its members is a newspaper writer
a fifth ... is a traitor working within

explanation.definitionFit: A regular newspaper writer belongs to the press, and a covert enemy sympathiser is a fifth one of the same word.

clue.text: Note's not about having a key

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the combined note and not are read backwards

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a musical note is not concerned with having a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses LA plus NOT as a whole, giving TON then AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal music is written in a definite key rather than atonally.

clue.text: Anything but 50% for sure

definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase means not a half share
a British slang retort meaning yes, very much so

explanation.definitionFit: Literally less or more than a half; colloquially an emphatic British way of saying absolutely.

clue.text: Heavy metal to belt a lot of drums in this

definitions.text: a lot of drums in this

parts.note: steel is a heavy metal
a band is a strap or belt

explanation.surface: A heavy metal fan bashes out a drum beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' suggests rock music; it is simply steel, and the definition is a Caribbean group playing oil-drum pans.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean ensemble playing pans made from oil drums.

clue.text: Shrewd spies lifted very old hat

parts.note: arch means knowing or shrewd

indicators.note: lifted means raised, so in a down clue the spies are read upwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Cunning agents stole a very old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' looks like stolen; in a down clue it turns CIA into AIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat means out of date, and something extremely antiquated is from a bygone era.

clue.text: Found rebuilding his stable

indicators.note: rebuilding means reconstructing, so the letters are put together anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discovered by reconstructing his horse barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; it is the verb to found, to set up.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a company is to set it up or institute it.

clue.text: Large building housing one child

indicators.note: housing means sheltering inside, so the barn contains the one

parts.note: a barn is a large farm building
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A big barn gives shelter to a single child.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRN is the Scottish word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a young child or infant.

clue.text: Moonshine's caught out by a fuss

indicators.note: out means taken away, so the cricket letter is removed

parts.note: hooch is illicit liquor, moonshine
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Bootleg whisky is found out and causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C from HOOCH, giving HOOH, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a commotion, an uproar about something.

clue.text: Sonically still, perhaps, but extremely masculine?

parts.note: the Mach number measures speed relative to sound
standing still is zero speed, so a zero is read as the letter O

explanation.surface: Quiet in sound, maybe, yet very manly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mach 0 is zero speed relative to sound, hence 'Sonically still'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes aggressively manly behaviour.

clue.text: One periodical that doesn't have first and last picture

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: lacking the first and last letters of the alphabet, A and Z, which are taken out of the periodical

parts.note: a magazine is a periodical

explanation.surface: A single magazine lacking its opening and closing pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and last' tempts you to strip the end letters of the word; it means A and Z of the alphabet, which 'doesn't have' removes from MAGAZINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form an image of it in the mind.

clue.text: Wise men right to interrupt 10 returning oriental art

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the whole assembled run is read backwards
the wise men plus right break into the numeral, sitting inside it

parts.note: the figures 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O
the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity

explanation.surface: Biblical sages interrupt a Midwest visit to admire Eastern art.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is not the cross-reference; it is IO. 'to interrupt' puts MAGIR inside, giving IMAGIRO, which 'returning' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of folding paper is an Eastern artform.

clue.text: The switch ain't electrified

indicators.note: switch means swap around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a light switch is not wired to the mains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like an electrical noun; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'the' is the grammatical determiner of English that specifies a noun.
